dedupe_keys.name: city of new orleans stormwater drainage system root cause analysis of the 2017 flooding abs group

description: This is the 158-page root cause analysis that ABS Group produced for the City of New Orleans after floods on 22 July, 5 August and 8 August 2017 left standing water over five feet deep for hours in many neighbourhoods, plus a turbine electrical fault on 9 August. It reports that three of four turbines that self-generate power for the drainage pumps were unavailable, leaving under 10 percent of designed self-produced power, that pump outages at two stations cut pumping to 45 to 70 percent of design, and that catch basins and drain lines were clogged or undersized. The method builds a cause and effect tree for the 5 August event and identifies causal, intermediate and root causes across budgeting, maintenance, human factors, leadership oversight and policy, and it makes recommended corrective actions. Coverage: one city's drainage and power system, one summer of events. Access: a free PDF on a state government site; the licence is not stated. Caveats: an institutional analysis with narrative findings, not modelled data; only the executive summary was read. It supports drainage pump capacity, power dependency and resilience modelling, and relates to the New Orleans levee case study and the Renton detention pond modelling case in the catalogue.
